subject: Scheduling: Hosted API connection patterns & tool/function calling deep-dive
summary: Customer requests a focused technical deep-dive to align on Hosted API integration patterns (SDKs, streaming, tool/function calling). We coordinate times, adjust for CET/PST, finalize agenda and invite CS to join for runbook discussion.

From: Eva Morales <eva@healthsync.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-18T16:12:00+01:00
Subject: Hosted API integration deep-dive — architecture review request

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering team at HealthSync would like a dedicated architecture session focused on how Redwood's Hosted API would fit into our ingestion and real-time scoring pipeline. Key areas we want covered:
- SDK integration patterns and auth flow
- streaming responses and latency characteristics for short-lived sessions
- tool/function calling (we have external medical lookup services to orchestrate)
- fallback strategies / model variants for graceful degradation

Can we schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week? Prefer afternoons CET (after 14:00 CET). I attached a short overview of our current architecture.

Attachment: healthsync-integration-overview.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

Best,
Eva Morales
Head of Integrations, HealthSync
eva@healthsync.ai
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Eva Morales <eva@healthsync.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-18T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API integration deep-dive — architecture review request

Hi Eva — great to hear from you and glad the demo was helpful. We can absolutely run a technical deep-dive that covers those topics. Proposed 60-minute slots (PST times shown, please convert to your local time):

- Tue Feb 22, 15:00–16:00 PST (Wed Feb 23, 00:00–01:00 CET)
- Wed Feb 23, 10:00–11:00 PST (Wed Feb 23, 19:00–20:00 CET)
- Thu Feb 24, 11:00–12:00 PST (Thu Feb 24, 20:00–21:00 CET)

Agenda I suggest: 1) 10–15m quick architecture sync (you), 2) 30–35m deep technical run-through (SDKs, streaming, tool calling examples, KV cache trade-offs), 3) 10–15m next steps + runbook/action items.

I'm looping in Karhtik (inference/runtime) and Marissa (solutions) so we can cover kernel/latency tradeoffs and integration patterns. If you prefer an earlier CET slot, let us know and we'll try to accommodate.

I attached our suggested architecture outline for the session.

Attachment: redwood-hosted-arch-outline.pdf (PDF, 640KB)

—
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.com
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Eva Morales <eva@healthsync.ai>
Date: 2027-02-18T10:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API integration deep-dive — architecture review request

Quick notes for the technical agenda (burn these in so we cover them in detail during the 'deep technical run-through'):

- SDK auth patterns: short-lived tokens vs long-lived keys; recommend short-lived with mTLS for private deploys.
- Streaming: sample throughput numbers for 1k concurrent short sessions (avg seq len 120 tokens). We'll bring a perf slide and live streaming demo using the JS client.
- KV cache: how prefix caching works across requests and what to expect when session affinity is lost.
- Tool/function calling: show a real example wiring an external medical lookup (sync vs async call patterns), error bubbling, and recommended idempotency keys for retries.
- Fallbacks: routing policy examples (model-variant vs region fallback) plus a brief note on quantized variants for cost trade-offs.

I recommend we make the session 75 minutes if HealthSync can spare the time — 50m tech + 25m for planning rollouts + Q&A. If not, we will keep to 60 and add a follow-up working session.

Sample snippet to discuss (we'll paste in full during the session):
const resp = await redwoodClient.stream({ model: 'rdw-3b', input: prompt, onToken: (t)=>console.log(t) })

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer, Principal Engineer — Runtime
